div.head: ECf 15.7
div.ab:
Si parentes non haberet, dominus eius eas haberet, aut felagus, si haberet, scilicet fide
ligatus cum eo. Si autem neutrum istorum haberet, rex regni, sub cuius dominio et pace degunt omnes albani, haberet VI marcas cum suis XL.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 641–642 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

Genoss versteht ein Interpolator der Retr. richtig. Etymologisch liegt Nord. félagi (Vermögensgenoss, Kamerad) vor; die Erklärung des Verfassers aus fei verräth den Franzosen
an interpolator of the Retr. rightly understands companion. Etymologically Norse félagi (partner in property, comrade) underlies it; the author’s explanation from fei betrays the Frenchman

Fremde, Franz. aubain, vom Retr. ausgelassen, vermuthlich weil unverstanden; 1138 nennen sich die Schotten Albani (Henr. Hunt.); und Aubanie heisst Anglofranz. im 12. Jahrh. Schottland (Fantosme). — Der König ist Schutzherr (der Juden ECf. 25) schon bei den Angelsachsen der Fremden, empfängt deren Nachlass (Birch Chart. Sax. 413) und theilweise das Wergeld Sippenloser; Ine 23; Af 28

foreigners, French aubain, left out by the Retractator, presumably because not understood; in 1138 the Scots call themselves Albani (Henry of Huntingdon); and in the 12th century Aubanie is Anglo-French for Scotland (Fantosme). — Already among the Anglo-Saxons the king is protector of foreigners (of the Jews, ECf. 25), receives their estate (Birch, Chart. Sax. 413) and in part the wergeld of those without kin; Ine 23; Af 28

div.ab: If he had no kinsmen, his lord should have them, or his felagus (fellow), if he had one, namely one bound with him by faith. But if he had neither of these, the king of the kingdom, under whose lordship and peace all aliens (albani) live, should have the six marks with his forty.
